name: arch-replace-ui
thesis: Replace forge/src/ui/ outright with a headless core plus an in-house signal/DOM component runtime, and do not open runner, storage, transport, budget or reconcile at all. Measured, the UI is only 16.9% of the minified bundle and 16 of 293 tests, while 22 of the 25 required components already have a data source below the seam - so the expensive, reviewed part of Forge is exactly the part that does not need to change. The cost is honest and large: roughly +125 KB minified, a new reconciler we own, and a temporary loss of the suite's thinnest coverage, which is why the first slice builds the test scaffold and the headless boundary before a single pixel moves.

ui_technology.choice: An in-house reactive DOM runtime: forge/src/ui/dom.mjs (kept) + forge/src/ui/reactive.mjs (new, ~140 lines). Components are plain factory functions (viewModel) => Element. No third-party UI dependency; the bundle stays a single esbuild IIFE.
ui_technology.why_not_preact: Preact implements dangerouslySetInnerHTML, which means its runtime assigns to .innerHTML. forge/build.mjs:33-37 greps the SHIPPED BUNDLE text (not just src/) for /\.innerHTML\s*=/ and /\binnerHTML\s*[:=]/ after stripping line comments, and throws. A minified `n.innerHTML=e` trips both. So adopting Preact forces one of three moves, each of which removes the guarantee: delete the gate, narrow it to src/ only (which is precisely the case it exists to catch - a dependency shipping a sink), or fork/patch Preact. It also adds a JSX compile step whose output is harder to read against the no-innerHTML law, and roughly +11 KB minified for preact plus ~3 KB for hooks. (Bundle numbers and the exact preact line are Inferred: preact is not in forge/node_modules and no package was fetched in this read-only pass. The gate mechanism and its regexes are Source-verified at build.mjs:33-37.)
ui_technology.why_not_lit: lit-html's mechanism IS an HTML string: a tagged template is joined into markup and assigned to a <template> element's innerHTML, then cloned. That is the dependency class the assignment says to reject, it trips the same build gate, and - worse - it makes 'no HTML string sink' unenforceable by grep, which is the only enforcement Forge has. Rejected on construction, not on size.
ui_technology.also_rejected: Solid (its web runtime clones from templates whose markup is assigned as a string, same gate problem) and micro-libraries such as van.js (a dependency for something measured at 3 KB in-house, with no DOM-only guarantee and no audit trail in this repository).
how_the_no_innerHTML_rule_holds: Construction: reactive.mjs has exactly two node-producing calls, document.createElement and document.createTextNode, and exactly one text-update path, node.data = String(value). There is no markup parser in the option at all.
Static gate kept: ui.test.mjs:29-34 walks every file under forge/src and fails on innerHTML|outerHTML|insertAdjacentHTML|document.write.
Build gate kept: build.mjs:33-37 re-greps the bundled output, so a future dependency cannot smuggle a sink past the src/ walk.
New runtime gate: h() gains a deny-list that throws on innerHTML/outerHTML/srcdoc/insertAdjacentHTML for ANY value type, closing the Behaviour-proven hole at dom.mjs:13 that both greps are blind to.

New stylesheet gate: the D2.4 contract test asserts every selector is scoped under .f-host/.f-app/.f-boot and that the sheet contains no url() and no @font-face, so the 'self-contained bundle' property is a test rather than a habit.
ui_technology.single_bundle_at_require_model: Unchanged. One esbuild IIFE at forge_bundle.js, one @require in forge_loader_user.js pinned to an immutable commit (forge_loader_user.js:12), promoted by release_pin.yml. The option adds no runtime fetch, no second @require, no CDN asset, no web font and no data URI pack. Because there is no third-party runtime, there is also no new supply-chain surface to audit per release.

bundle_size_estimate.method: Measured, then projected from measured densities. (1) Baseline re-derived in this pass with esbuild 0.28.2 minify:true + metafile per-input attribution over forge/src/main.mjs: total 232,708 B minified, gzip 52,556 (matches A.9's 232,720/52,556 to 12 bytes; the shipped bundle is minify:false at 397,984 B / 74,897 gzip, also re-measured). (2) UI subtotal measured at 39,342 B minified = 16.9% of the bundle: screens.mjs 18,304, app.mjs 11,899, styles.mjs 5,283, takeover.mjs 2,326, dom.mjs 1,530. (3) Derived contract data measured at 96,200 B minified = 41.3%: nested.json 77,735, 32b_DATA_pool.json 11,792, fields.json 6,673. (4) The new runtime was written and measured, not guessed: the 136-line prototype at scratchpad/design/proto/runtime.mjs bundles to 2,996 B minified / 1,360 gzip and contains no innerHTML. (5) Densities measured from today's UI: render code 55.6 minified B per source line (screens.mjs), orchestration 29.0 (app.mjs), CSS 0.85 minified B per source byte (styles.mjs).
bundle_size_estimate.projection: runtime 3.0 KB + CSS (D2.7 estimates 16-20 KB of source; at 0.85 -> ~17 KB) + 25 WCM component factories at ~90 lines each x 45 B/line -> ~101 KB + ~12 destinations at ~60 lines x 45 -> ~32 KB + view-model/presenter code ~400 lines x 30 -> ~12 KB = about 165 KB minified for the UI layer, with an honest range of 120-200 KB.
bundle_size_estimate.net: 232.7 - 39.3 + 165 = about 358 KB minified, gzip about 81 KB at today's measured 4.43:1 code ratio. Unminified that is roughly 600-620 KB, which is why this option treats K-14 (ship a minified bundle) as a phase-0 dependency rather than a nicety. For scale: the Quest Studio seam alone is +39,621 B unminified (+10.0%, A.9).
levers_named_honestly: K-14 minify: -165 KB against the shipped artifact today; the single largest lever and a user decision, not mine.

Lazy contract parse: main.mjs:21-22 imports nested.json and fields.json as JSON modules, which esbuild inlines as JS object literals evaluated at module init - on EVERY game page the loader matches, even though boot() returns early on unarmed pages (A.9). Shipping them as JSON string literals parsed on first validator use removes that boot work. Measured: JSON.parse of minified nested.json is 0.245 ms per call on this machine (20 iterations, node), so the saving is sub-millisecond on desktop and plausibly 1-3 ms on the phone. Modest, real, and it costs no bytes - I am not claiming it is the answer to R-06.
Transfer cost is not the problem: nested.json gzips to 2,922 B, fields.json 2,283 B, pool 3,563 B - 8.8 KB of the 52.6 KB gzip total. Parse and memory are the cost, and @require caches the bytes.

A CI ceiling gate (raw and gzip, asserted in build.mjs or a test) per phase, so growth is a decision rather than a discovery. forge.yml already proves bundle reproducibility; the ceiling is one more assertion in the same job.

ui_technology.how_screens_become_testable: Every component is a pure factory (viewModel) => Element with no facade access and no closure over live state; the view-model is a plain serializable object produced by src/core/viewmodels.mjs. A UI-contract test therefore needs no compose(), no FakeGame and no IndexedDB - it builds a fixture view-model, calls the factory in jsdom, and serializes the subtree deterministically (tag, sorted attributes, text) into a committed fixture under forge/test/fixtures/screens/. Because h() builds real nodes with no innerHTML, that serialization is stable, and the diff is reviewed in CI exactly as the tRPC envelope fixtures already are (forge.yml fixture-reproducibility job). Full-screen tests keep the existing selectors (.f-app, .f-nav, .f-main, .f-pill.<STATE>) so ui.test.mjs:86-105 and :234-284 survive the replacement rather than being rewritten with it.

storage_migration.journal_v1_to_v2: This option does NOT introduce journal v2. The one new durable fact it needs - repository sync state for a results bundle (A.4.1 item 4, H R-07) - is written with the existing journal.annotateJob (journal.mjs:349-354) as job.sync = {state, at, path, error}. Verified safe in both directions in this pass: validateJobShape (journal.mjs:151-162) checks only jobId, items array, job.state and per-item idx/state, so it accepts unknown top-level keys; migrate() (journal.mjs:407-423) keys only on job.v; annotateJob refuses only items/state/jobId/v. So a previous pinned bundle reads a job carrying `sync` without error and ignores it, and MIGRATIONS stays empty. If a later phase genuinely needs v2, H R-09's rules apply unchanged: additive step, fixtures from real exported journals, never delete a v1 record on failure (park under <key>.corrupt as compat.mjs already does).
storage_migration.indexeddb: tnr_forge v2 -> v3, additive, in exactly the pattern captures.mjs:33-35 already documents for v1 -> v2. v3 adds one store, `packages`, keyed by `${path}@${sha}`, for manifest and workstream text. This retires the design smell A.5 records: today App.loadPicker writes repository text into the GAME read cache under the synthetic path 'github.contents' (app.mjs:198-200), where CapturesScreen lists it as if it were a capture and 'Clear all' deletes it (ui.test.mjs:206-232 exercises that Clear all path). The existing `captures` and `capture_snapshots` stores, their keys and their lifetimes are untouched. Migration on upgrade: the v3 upgrade creates the store and does NOT copy the old github.contents rows - they are a cache, re-fetchable, and copying them would import the smell into the new store. A one-time sweep deletes rows whose path is 'github.contents' from `captures` so the Captures destination stops listing repository text as evidence.
storage_migration.retained_builder_keys: tnr_bk_idmap_v1 and tnr_bk_gh_v1 are read and written through storage/compat.mjs exactly as today (app.mjs:215,395,400 call sites move to core/, the key names and shapes do not change). Builder v4.32 keeps working on the same device: it is not deprecated (brief section 16) and it is still the only tool for the 7 hard blockers in B.3.1.

New UI-only preferences (reduce motion, daylight, classic-shell flag) go in one key tnr_forge_ui_v1 behind try/catch, and every one of them has a correct default when the read throws or returns null.
storage_migration.rollback: Reinstall the previously pinned loader (forge_loader_user.js @require is an immutable commit; release_pin.yml is the only promoter). Because the journal stays v1 and the IDB upgrade is additive, a downgrade is lossless: the old bundle reads every job, ignores job.sync, and does not know about the `packages` store (IDB refuses to DOWNGRADE a database version, so the old bundle opening tnr_forge at version 2 while the stored version is 3 fails its open - this is the one real rollback hazard and it is why CaptureCache must treat an open failure as a degraded-but-usable state rather than a fatal one; app.mjs:277 and :372-379 already model that for the export path and the same discipline is carried into core/evidence.mjs). Marked Inferred: the exact IndexedDB downgrade behaviour on Firefox Android was not exercised in this read-only pass, and it belongs in the user's device smoke for the phase that raises the version.

release_strategy.bundles: One. forge_bundle.js stays a single esbuild IIFE and forge_loader_user.js keeps exactly one @require pinned to an immutable commit (forge_loader_user.js:12). No second @require, no runtime module fetch, no CDN asset. The loader's @match, @run-at document-start and the per-tab arm marker are unchanged.
release_strategy.lazy_contract_data: Not a second file and not a network fetch. fields.json and nested.json move from JSON-module imports (main.mjs:21-22, inlined by esbuild as object literals evaluated at module init) to string literals parsed on first use by Validator. Measured context: they are 84,758 B of the 232,708 B minified bundle but only 5.2 KB gzipped, so this buys boot work and heap, not transfer. It is worth doing because A.9 records that the parse is paid on every game page the loader matches even though boot() returns early on unarmed pages - but it is a small win and this option does not pretend otherwise.
release_strategy.loader_and_pin: Phase-per-release. Each of the 5 slices below is its own release SHA, so the operator can roll back to the previous pinned loader at any point without a data migration. Settings shows the bundle commit and the game-source pin (A.6) so the device can be identified from a screenshot. One blocker must be cleared in phase 0: release_loader.test.mjs:47 demands exactly one @x-release-pending marker, which release_pin.yml removes on main, so every main checkout is red (292/293) and CI never sees it because the bot commit does not trigger forge.yml (H R-11, re-measured in this pass). The fix already exists on the ChatGPT branch (824c4d58 relaxes it to 'at most one') and is coupled there to unrelated loader-assertion rewrites (H R-22). That coupling is CF-19: who authors the fix is the director's call, and this option does not author a competing release_loader change.
release_strategy.ci: One Node workflow with one gate set (audit, test, fixture reproducibility, bundle reproducibility, size ceiling, stylesheet contract). forge.yml's paths must gain push/**/*.json and state/staged_workflows/release_pin.yml, which runner.test.mjs:320-328 and check_release_pin.mjs:18 already read (deep-dive note).

recovery.principle: Recovery is a destination, not a toast (brief section 15). Every state that must persist until resolved is rendered from the journal on mount, so a crash, an eviction or a closed tab loses only in-memory convenience.
recovery.tab_eviction_or_crash_mid_job: Unchanged mechanics: the journal wrote SENT before the request (journal.mjs:330-335), the lease is a 30 s heartbeat (runner.mjs:40), pre-create id snapshots are in localStorage (reconciler.mjs:68). On the next mount the shell reads journal.resumable() and journal.ambiguous() and lands the operator on the Recovery destination with the SENT banner, the candidates and the two legal actions (Reconcile & resume, Adopt/Skip). What changes is that this is a destination with a badge on the shell rather than a warn banner on the Jobs screen (screens.mjs:16-27). What must NOT change: no control anywhere is labelled Retry, because SENT -> PLANNED is structurally impossible (journal.mjs:41) and run() refuses a job with SENT items (runner.mjs:193). A UI-contract test asserts that no rendered control in any state calls a send path while an item is SENT (H R-01).
recovery.the_new_risk_this_option_introduces: A reactive UI holds live subscriptions; an evicted or reloaded tab must not resurrect stale in-memory state. proposal.q1: REPLACE the UI layer; preserve runner, storage, transport, budget and reconcile. Evidence for 'replace' rather than 'evolve': (a) the UI is a small, separable fraction of the artefact - measured in this pass at 39,342 of 232,708 minified bytes (16.9%), and 277 of the 293 tests never touch it; (b) the capability work is already done below the seam - A.12 shows 22 of 25 WCM components have a Forge data source today and only three states are missing (sync half of ResultSummary, authorization denial, a structured waiting-for-response event), so this is a presentation problem, which is exactly what the UX audit concluded ('weaknesses are presentation, not safety'); (c) evolving in place cannot fix the two structural defects - ui/app.mjs mixes domain logic with rendering (harvestEntry :29, blockedPaths :166, resolveCaptures :323-366, exportJob :369) so the leak that blocks q3 survives any in-place refactor, and screens.mjs re-renders whole screens on a 1.5 s setInterval (app.mjs:268) which cannot host 25 stateful components; (d) the defects that must change are class defects, not instances - styles.mjs:44 paints DONE green regardless of jobOutcome, screens.mjs:86 and :146 reuse outcome pills for non-outcome meaning, .f-nav 40 px and .f-exit 32 px sit under the touch floor. Cost of replace, stated plainly: the 16 UI tests are the thinnest part of the suite (textContent regexes, several buttons never clicked), so replacing the UI temporarily removes more protection than it looks like, which is why R0 builds the test scaffold before R2 touches the shell.
proposal.q2: The vanilla DOM/CSSOM constraints remain REQUIRED, and this option strengthens them rather than trading them for ergonomics. A component strategy is still adopted - components are pure (viewModel) => Element factories over a 140-line signal runtime measured at 2,996 B minified - so maintainability improves without a framework. The constraint is load-bearing for three verified reasons: (1) the no-innerHTML law is enforced by grep in two places, ui.test.mjs:29-34 over src/ and build.mjs:33-37 over the SHIPPED BUNDLE, and the bundle grep is precisely what a third-party runtime would trip; (2) the overlay mounts on a live game route, so the stylesheet must stay scoped to .f-host/.f-app and survive Close (styles.mjs:1-9, takeover.mjs:177-182) - a framework that installs global styles or its own root is a carrier-contamination risk (H R-28); (3) the single @require model rewards zero dependencies: no per-release supply-chain audit, no version pin beyond the repo's own. Preact is rejected because dangerouslySetInnerHTML means its runtime assigns .innerHTML, which trips build.mjs and forces us to weaken the gate (Inferred on the library internals - preact is not installed and nothing was fetched; Source-verified on the gate). lit is rejected on construction: its mechanism is an HTML string assigned to a template's innerHTML, which is the dependency class the assignment says to reject and which makes the law unenforceable by grep. Cost of in-house: we own reconciler bugs, there are no devtools, and the keyed-list code is new and unproven - which is why it ships in R1 behind the existing five screens before any new screen depends on it.
proposal.q3: The seam already exists at compose() (main.mjs:35-57) and everything below ui/ is injectable; A.2 records that the leakage runs the other way. This option makes the seam consumable by adding src/core/ - facades, a typed event set and serializable snapshots - and moving the eight pieces of domain logic out of app.mjs (listed in core_api.logic_leaving_app_mjs with line cites). The boundary is proven, not asserted: a static test forbids any DOM global under src/core/, and R4 runs the whole core in node with a text renderer against recorded fixtures. One honest limit: JobProgress needs a structured 'waiting for response' event that the runner does not emit today (A.12), and this option does NOT add it, because that is a runner-side Lane A change and the assignment preserves the runner. Until it lands, the UI renders phase from the journal write (SENT) and from the runner's existing log(msg, item) callback, and says nothing the machine does not hold.
proposal.q5: This option does NOT introduce journal v2. The one new durable fact it needs - repository sync state for a results bundle (A.4.1 item 4, H R-07) - is written with the existing journal.annotateJob (journal.mjs:349-354) as job.sync = {state, at, path, error}. Verified safe in both directions in this pass: validateJobShape (journal.mjs:151-162) checks only jobId, items array, job.state and per-item idx/state, so it accepts unknown top-level keys; migrate() (journal.mjs:407-423) keys only on job.v; annotateJob refuses only items/state/jobId/v. So a previous pinned bundle reads a job carrying `sync` without error and ignores it, and MIGRATIONS stays empty. If a later phase genuinely needs v2, H R-09's rules apply unchanged: additive step, fixtures from real exported journals, never delete a v1 record on failure (park under <key>.corrupt as compat.mjs already does). IndexedDB: tnr_forge v2 -> v3, additive, in exactly the pattern captures.mjs:33-35 already documents for v1 -> v2. v3 adds one store, `packages`, keyed by `${path}@${sha}`, for manifest and workstream text. This retires the design smell A.5 records: today App.loadPicker writes repository text into the GAME read cache under the synthetic path 'github.contents' (app.mjs:198-200), where CapturesScreen lists it as if it were a capture and 'Clear all' deletes it (ui.test.mjs:206-232 exercises that Clear all path). The existing `captures` and `capture_snapshots` stores, their keys and their lifetimes are untouched. Migration on upgrade: the v3 upgrade creates the store and does NOT copy the old github.contents rows - they are a cache, re-fetchable, and copying them would import the smell into the new store. A one-time sweep deletes rows whose path is 'github.contents' from `captures` so the Captures destination stops listing repository text as evidence. Rollback: Reinstall the previously pinned loader (forge_loader_user.js @require is an immutable commit; release_pin.yml is the only promoter). Because the journal stays v1 and the IDB upgrade is additive, a downgrade is lossless: the old bundle reads every job, ignores job.sync, and does not know about the `packages` store (IDB refuses to DOWNGRADE a database version, so the old bundle opening tnr_forge at version 2 while the stored version is 3 fails its open - this is the one real rollback hazard and it is why CaptureCache must treat an open failure as a degraded-but-usable state rather than a fatal one; app.mjs:277 and :372-379 already model that for the export path and the same discipline is carried into core/evidence.mjs). Marked Inferred: the exact IndexedDB downgrade behaviour on Firefox Android was not exercised in this read-only pass, and it belongs in the user's device smoke for the phase that raises the version.
proposal.q7: Unchanged by this option, and deliberately so. transport/procedures.mjs stays the 43-row audited registry transcribed from the pin (procedures.mjs:13-22) and anything outside it still throws before any fetch. Registry expansion to cover real research reads (combat.getBattleHistory, combat.getBattleEntries, gameAsset.getAllFolders) is B.5 gate G-02 and K-17, a separate Lane A slice with its own auth transcription and ChatGPT review; a UI replacement must not smuggle it in. What the UI layer owes the drift problem is one rule: every procedure path, limiter class and auth class the UI shows is READ FROM PROCEDURES, never re-typed in a component - the generated-projection discipline RUL-2026-09-12-002 and RB section 4 demand, and the exact pattern H R-20 flags in the Studio's browser-side shape rules. A UI-contract test fails if a component names a procedure path that PROCEDURES does not carry. Drift gates themselves stay where they are: pin_relevance.mjs run against the game head of the day as a phase-0 gate, with the pin SHA rendered in Settings so a device can be identified.
proposal.q11: Discovery becomes one facade, core.packages, with three sources behind it and one presentation: (a) push/*.json on main, which is all the picker lists today (app.mjs:186-207, github.mjs:33); (b) state/workstreams/<slug>/roadmap.json rendered READ-ONLY as the project context a work package belongs to, which is the 'load project/source' operation RB section 6 names; (c) later, Studio builds, once the promotion contract exists (K-39). Three constraints this option accepts rather than resolves: Forge may PROJECT workstream state but how much of it Forge may EDIT is K-28 and stays open; the roadmap packet is a deterministic view of coordination state and not an authority (CLAUDE.md section 2), so the UI shows it with its source revision and never as a second canon; and the Studio's builds land on studio/quest/<id> while the picker lists push/ on main (A.8 item 6), so until K-39 is ruled the relay persists and the UI must say so honestly rather than offering a promotion button that does not exist. Cost: workstream reads spend GitHub API quota, not game budget, and they must be cache-first in the new `packages` store with an explicit refresh tap and a visible age - the same discipline H R-03 imposes on game reads.
proposal.q12: Two changes, both fixing measured breakage, neither altering the shape harvest.py already reads. (1) `checks` must stop being null. A Forge bundle carries checks: null (app.mjs:382); validate.py --parity does set(bundle.get('checks', [])) and raises TypeError; session_close.py --guards runs parity on the lexically newest inbox bundle, so the content session's close guard is red whenever a Forge bundle is newest (H R-19, Behaviour-proven on tnr_results_1789124514980.json). core/bundle.mjs emits a real checks inventory from the validator and lints it ALREADY RAN, which is the honest option; the alternative (make parity skip cfg:'forge' bundles) is cheaper and is a user decision, not mine. (2) Sync state joins the bundle and the journal as job.sync, so 'live verified but repository not synced' is a distinguishable state rather than a vanished toast (A.4.1 item 4, H R-07, CPY section 14). Everything else is frozen: state, outcome, forgeState, verdict, postflight, entries, captures, idmap, journal keep their keys and their meanings, and harvest.test.mjs (8 tests, 7 shelling out to the real harvest.py) is the gate that says so. Two contract gaps this option does NOT close and must not pretend to: Forge bundles carry no list `data`, so they never feed answers/ (build_answers.py), and they carry no pushed/live pair - both are B.3 gate G-03 work.
proposal.q13: The journal is the audit record and stays the audit record; this option adds surfaces, not stores. What becomes visible: an Activity destination reading journal.listJobs() with the real outcome per run (not a free-coloured dot); job.sync so 'what happened to the evidence' is part of the history; journal.broken rendered for the first time (today it exists only inside the text export, A.4.1 item 5); the manifest hash, the bundle commit SHA and the game-source pin shown per run so a run can be reproduced. What this option explicitly does NOT invent: an approval/audit trail for content administration. Where approval state lives is K-09, the game has no native approval field, and E_CONTENT_ADMIN_FEASIBILITY owns the source audit. Also unresolved and left open: retention - nothing is deleted automatically (non-negotiable), and 'Delete finished jobs' keeps INCOMPLETE and PAUSED jobs (screens.mjs:322), which the new MaintenanceAction component must state in its label rather than imply.
proposal.q14: Measured, then projected. Baseline re-derived in this pass: shipped bundle 397,984 B raw / 74,897 gzip (minify:false); the same source at minify:true is 232,708 B / 52,556 gzip. Per-input attribution (esbuild metafile): derived contract data 96,200 B minified (41.3%) - nested.json 77,735, 32b_DATA_pool.json 11,792, fields.json 6,673 - and the whole UI layer 39,342 B (16.9%). The new runtime was written and measured rather than estimated: 2,996 B minified / 1,360 gzip for 136 source lines, with no innerHTML in the output. Projection for a 25-component, ~12-destination UI at today's measured densities (55.6 minified B per source line for render code, 0.85 per source byte for CSS): about 165 KB minified for the UI layer, range 120-200 KB, giving about 358 KB minified / ~81 KB gzip for the bundle, or roughly 600-620 KB unminified. That is a real cost and it is the strongest argument against this option; three things bound it. (1) K-14 (minify) is worth -165 KB against today's shipped artefact and is a user decision this option depends on rather than assumes. (2) A CI ceiling on raw and gzip bytes per phase, in the same job that already proves bundle reproducibility, so growth is decided rather than discovered. (3) The contract data, not the UI, is the startup cost today: main.mjs:21-22 imports nested.json and fields.json as JSON modules, which esbuild inlines as object literals evaluated at module init on EVERY game page the loader matches even though boot() returns early on unarmed pages (A.9). Parsing them lazily from string literals removes that work; measured JSON.parse of minified nested.json is 0.245 ms per call on this machine, so the saving is sub-millisecond on desktop and plausibly a few milliseconds on the phone - honest, modest, and not a substitute for the ceiling. Transfer is not the issue: the three data files gzip to 8.8 KB of the 52.6 KB total and @require caches them. No device measurement was made; every phone claim here is Inferred and belongs in the user's smoke.
proposal.q15: One. forge_bundle.js stays a single esbuild IIFE and forge_loader_user.js keeps exactly one @require pinned to an immutable commit (forge_loader_user.js:12). Each of the 5 slices below is its own release SHA, so the operator can roll back to the previous pinned loader at any point without a data migration. weaknesses: Bundle growth is the strongest argument against this option: about +125 KB minified for the UI layer, taking the artefact to roughly 358 KB minified / 600-620 KB unminified, parsed on every game page the loader matches. It makes H R-06 worse, not better, and it depends on K-14 (minify), which is a user decision I cannot settle.

The size projection is a projection. Only the runtime (2,996 B) and the baseline were measured; the 25-component figure comes from today's measured source-line density applied to an assumed component size, with a stated range of 120-200 KB. If components run larger than 90 lines the number moves, and nothing here proves they will not.

Replace is a bigger bet than evolve on the one axis where the evidence is thinnest: the UI tests. 16 tests, textContent regexes, several buttons never clicked. Phase R0 builds the scaffold first, but between R2 and R3 the new shell carries more behaviour than the old test set ever protected.

The in-house runtime means we own a reconciler. A keyed-list bug is our bug, with no ecosystem, no devtools and no second user to find it. Preact would have been the safer code; it is the no-innerHTML gate, not the code quality, that rules it out.

It closes none of the 7 hard retirement blockers (B.3.1). Zip packs, research reads outside the registry, paged list captures with bodies, srcId idempotency and retry-a-failed-step are all untouched, so Builder stays installed and the parity clock does not move at all because of this option.

Two of the three A.12 'no source' states stay unsourced: authorization denial needs the K-34 audit and a structured signal, and JobProgress's 'waiting for response' needs a runner-side change this option refuses to make. The UI will therefore be honest but coarser than the component map wants.

The Studio seam is owned by another writer and is not integrated here. If its independent review lands changes to dom.mjs's h() (824c4d58 already changes the value-assignment branch), the deny-list I propose has to be reconciled with it, and that is a merge this plan does not schedule.

The IndexedDB v2 -> v3 rise makes rollback one-way for the cache: an older pinned bundle cannot open a higher-versioned database. I have designed around it (degraded-but-usable cache open) but I did not exercise it, and Firefox Android behaviour here is Inferred.

Every device-facing claim is Inferred. No browser was opened, no phone was measured, adoptedStyleSheets/glyph coverage/OS preference forwarding/persist() are all unverified, and the responsive half of the visual system cannot be tested in jsdom at all.

The five slices assume a single writer on forge/src/ui/ for their whole duration. Concurrent content work does not conflict, but any other Lane A UI slice does, and the plan has no answer for that except the one-writer rule.
